After the prewash the residual water may be discharged into the sea subject to the discharge conditions. Additional restrictions apply in special areas. Extinguishing: foam, CO₂, dry powder. Class C: flammable gases (LPG, natural gas). Extinguishing: dry powder. The gas supply must be shut off. Class D: combustible metals (magnesium, aluminium powder). Extinguishing: special dry powder. Class E (electrical fire): electrical equipment. Extinguishing: CO₂, dry powder. Water is not used. Combustible wastes accumulated on board.en: Combustible wastes accumulated on board (oily sludge, oil residues, some garbage) are burned in the incinerator to reduce their volume; this lowers the quantity of waste that has to be landed ashore.

DEFINITION OF HEAVY LIFT: Generally carg.en: DEFINITION OF HEAVY LIFT: Generally cargoes weighing more than 50 tonnes as a single piece. Transformers, generators, industrial equipment and cranes fall into this category.

Figure-of-eight knot: tied in the end of.en: Figure-of-eight knot: tied in the end of a rope to stop it running out of a block or sheave. A simple and effective stopper knot.

For Category X a prewash and verificatio.en: For Category X a prewash and verification of the residue concentration are required.

Fuel (bunker) cost constitutes the large.en: Fuel (bunker) cost constitutes the largest item of voyage expenses and directly affects freight profitability.

GZ (the righting lever) is the horizonta.en: GZ (the righting lever) is the horizontal distance between the centre of gravity (G) and the line of action of the buoyancy force when the ship is heeled through a given angle. This lever produces the righting moment and shows the ship's tendency to return upright.

Great circle geometry forms the core of.en: Great circle geometry forms the core of the navigational mathematics that treats the earth as a sphere. The arc where the single plane through two positions and the centre of the earth cuts the sphere is the great circle arc. A great circle is therefore not an arbitrary curve but a fully determined geometric necessity.

Harbour tow: a short towline, low speed,.en: Harbour tow: a short towline, low speed, tug control. Ocean tow: a long towline (500-1000 m), where the catenary matters; the tow can last for days.

If a \"clearly hazardous\" deficiency is.en: If a "clearly hazardous" deficiency is found on board the ship is detained. Detention causes serious financial and reputational loss to the ship operator. Detention rates directly affect the targeting profile of the company and the flag State.

If the weight removed was high up, KG de.en: If the weight removed was high up, KG decreases and stability may improve; if weight is removed from low down, KG rises and stability decreases. The consumption and discharge plan must therefore be watched carefully from the stability point of view.

In refrigerated carriage some of the gas.en: In refrigerated carriage some of the gas evaporates because of heat ingress (boil-off gas, BOG). On LPG carriers a reliquefaction plant returns the BOG to liquid; on LNG carriers the BOG is mostly used as fuel in the machinery.

In shipping, supply is inelastic in the.en: In shipping, supply is inelastic in the short term (building a new ship takes 2-4 years); changes in demand therefore cause extreme volatility in prices.

Increases the risk of the cargo shifting.en: Increases the risk of the cargo shifting

Initial stability is the stability of th.en: Initial stability is the stability of the ship at small angles of heel from upright (generally up to 10°). Within this range the metacentre (M) is taken as fixed.

Intermediate values are kept at full pre.en: Intermediate values are kept at full precision in the calculation engine; the rounding shown is not carried into the next step. Verify the results against the ship-specific approved documentation and instrument output.

JUMPING (a last resort): from no more th.en: JUMPING (a last resort): from no more than 5 metres. The lifejacket must be firmly secured. Cover the mouth and nose with one hand. Hold the lifejacket down with the other hand. Keep the feet together. Jump upright. Jump from the lee side. Jump at least 3 metres clear of the ship (suction effect).

Jumping into the sea from the ship is a.en: Jumping into the sea from the ship is a last resort. If you must jump: the lifejacket is secured tightly, the mouth and nose are covered with one hand, the feet are held together and the jump is from no more than 5 metres. Jump from the lee side.

KB is the distance from the keel to the.en: KB is the distance from the keel to the centre of buoyancy and depends on the immersed shape. BM is the ratio of the waterplane moment of inertia to the immersed volume. KG is the height of the centre of gravity above the keel.

KG: the distance from the keel to the ce.en: KG: the distance from the keel to the centre of gravity (from the loading calculation)

LCG: the longitudinal centre of gravity.en: LCG: the longitudinal centre of gravity (important for trim)

Leakage scenarios: sensitivity analyses.en: Leakage scenarios: sensitivity analyses covering the free surface, KG change and heeling moment effects in the event of a cargo leak.

Lifting a weight with a crane, placing e.en: Lifting a weight with a crane, placing equipment on deck or transferring ballast to the bottom tanks are all vertical weight movements. In particular, when a weight is suspended the effective position of its centre of gravity is taken as having moved to the point of suspension.

Manoeuvring and warning signals (Rule 34.en: Manoeuvring and warning signals (Rule 34): one short blast = altering to starboard, two short = altering to port, five short = doubt/warning.

Manoeuvring: steering, transits of narro.en: Manoeuvring: steering, transits of narrow waters, berthing and unberthing.

Mechanical ventilation: forced air circu.en: Mechanical ventilation: forced air circulation by fans and blowers. Used in the engine room, the pump room and large cargo holds.

NOTE: the SHAPE does not change between.en: NOTE: the SHAPE does not change between regions. The port hand mark is cylindrical (can) in both regions and the starboard hand mark is conical in both. So when the colour cannot be made out (at night, in fog or at a distance), the shape and topmark still give the right information.

NOx formation is not obtained from a clo.en: NOx formation is not obtained from a closed analytical relation; compliance is determined by comparing the weighted NOx value measured over the NOx Technical Code test cycle with the speed-dependent Tier limit.

OPEN MOOR: The two anchors are laid at a.en: OPEN MOOR: The two anchors are laid at an angle of 60-90°; this limits the swing and improves holding when the current/wind changes direction.

On chemical tankers when changing grade..en: On chemical tankers when changing grade. Selecting the right cleaning agent is critical.

On tankers and in spaces with a risk of.en: On tankers and in spaces with a risk of a flammable atmosphere, gas measurement (gas-free/gas testing) is mandatory; a gas-free certificate is obtained.

Open loop: washes with the natural alkal.en: Open loop: washes with the natural alkalinity of seawater; after monitoring, the washwater is discharged into the sea.

Parametric rolling arises from the perio.en: Parametric rolling arises from the periodic change in the ship's waterplane area as a wave passes. When the wave crest is amidships the waterplane area decreases (GM falls); in the trough the waterplane area increases (GM rises). Under certain conditions this variation in GM creates resonance.

Placing bagged grain on the cargo surfac.en: Placing bagged grain on the cargo surface of a partly filled hold. Covering the surface with a minimum of 16 bags (150 mm thickness).

Post a lookout – do not lose sight of th.en: Post a lookout – do not lose sight of the person in the water

Safe speed considering visibility, traff.en: Safe speed considering visibility, traffic, manoeuvrability and radar limitations.

Sailing vessel: sidelights and sternligh.en: Sailing vessel: sidelights and sternlight only. Optional: red over green all-round lights at the masthead.

Static stability examines the equilibriu.en: Static stability examines the equilibrium of the ship at a given angle of heel. The analysis is made for a condition in which there is no motion, that is, in which the ship is treated as "frozen" at that angle.

The load lines are used together with the seasonal zones on the world chart (tropical, summer, winter, seasonal areas); the ship must not exceed the line appropriate to the zone and season it is in.

The HRU is activated automatically by wa.en: The HRU is activated automatically by water pressure when the ship sinks to a depth of 2-4 metres. It releases the securing strap, the raft floats to the surface and inflates automatically as the painter comes taut. The liferaft is serviced at an approved station every 12 months; the HRU is a disposable item that is not serviced and is renewed by the expiry date marked on it, normally every 2 years.

The IS Code criteria form the baseline;.en: The IS Code criteria form the baseline; depending on the cargo and personnel density, Administrations generally require a minimum GM ≥ 0.15 m.

The LCB (Longitudinal Centre of Buoyancy.en: The LCB (Longitudinal Centre of Buoyancy) is the longitudinal centre of the immersed volume. The buoyancy force acts upwards through this point.

The LCF (Longitudinal Centre of Flotatio.en: The LCF (Longitudinal Centre of Flotation) is the longitudinal position of the centre of flotation.

The LCG (Longitudinal Centre of Gravity).en: The LCG (Longitudinal Centre of Gravity) is the longitudinal resultant of all the weights on the ship, calculated by the method of moments.

The OWS discharge oil concentration must.en: The OWS discharge oil concentration must be ≤ 15 ppm (15 ppm alarm + automatic stopping device).

The acceleration factors (longitudinal,.en: The acceleration factors (longitudinal, transverse, vertical) are selected from the Annex 13 tables according to the ship's length and service speed.

The berthing plan is made according to t.en: The berthing plan is made according to the wind, current, tide, water depth (UKC) and the layout of the berth. The roles and the plan are shared in a manoeuvring briefing (the master/pilot exchange).

The boat slides down the ramp and enters.en: The boat slides down the ramp and enters the water in free fall.

The buddy system (working in pairs) is m.en: The buddy system (working in pairs) is mandatory; the team is monitored from outside.

The buoyancy force (B) – acting upwards.en: The buoyancy force (B) – acting upwards through the centre of buoyancy (B)

The buoyancy force is equal to the weigh.en: The buoyancy force is equal to the weight of the water displaced by the immersed volume of the ship. It acts upwards through the centre of buoyancy (B) and keeps the ship afloat by balancing its weight.

The centre of buoyancy (B) is the geomet.en: The centre of buoyancy (B) is the geometric centre of the ship's immersed volume. This point moves when the ship heels because the shape of the immersed volume changes.

The centre of gravity G is the resultant.en: The centre of gravity G is the resultant point of all the weights on the ship, calculated by the method of moments.

The conning officer gives clear, single.en: The conning officer gives clear, single orders; only one person gives orders at any time. Even with a pilot on board the responsibility remains with the master; orders are still given and acknowledged in the standard form.

The deck scuppers are checked clear.en: The deck scuppers are checked clear

The master is responsible overall for ca.en: The master is responsible overall for cargo operations. The chief officer manages the day-to-day cargo operations and prepares the loading plan.

The metacentre (M) is the point at which.en: The metacentre (M) is the point at which the vertical drawn through the new position of the centre of buoyancy (B), when the ship heels through a very small angle, intersects the ship's centreline. This point determines whether or not a righting moment is produced at small angles.

The new centre of gravity is calculated.en: The new centre of gravity is calculated by the method of moments. The vertical (kg), transverse (tcg) and longitudinal (lcg) positions of the added weight are each assessed separately. This is essential at every loading step in order to stay within the limits of the stability book.

The new position of the centre of buoyan.en: The new position of the centre of buoyancy (B) is found.

The permit system is operated in line wi.en: The permit system is operated in line with the ISM/SMS procedures and PSC inspections; the records are audited.

The photo is processed by AI to read the.en: The photo is processed by AI to read the dates and is kept in your private account archive. The results do not replace the official document; low-confidence readings are marked clearly.

The point about which the ship turns lie.en: The point about which the ship turns lies close to the bow when going ahead and close to the stern when going astern. The turning moment produced by the rudder and the tugs is assessed relative to the pivot point.

The position and the way the ship is agr.en: The position and the way the ship is aground are established (draft readings).

The position of the metacentre is determ.en: The position of the metacentre is determined by the distance BM, calculated from the waterplane moment of inertia and the immersed volume. BM is the vertical distance between B and M and is sensitive to the shape of the waterplane.

The pressure is entered in bar and conve.en: The pressure is entered in bar and converted to 10⁵ Pa in the calculation; the diameter is entered in mm.

The signals for vessels restricted in th.en: The signals for vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre and not under command (Rule 27) must be displayed correctly.

The tank atmosphere must not be within t.en: The tank atmosphere must not be within the flammable range. The inert gas system (IGS) makes the atmosphere non-combustible by reducing the oxygen in the tank (generally below 8% by volume); this is the basis of ISGOTT operations.

HOW DOES AN EPIRB APPEAR ON RADAR? A sta.en: HOW DOES AN EPIRB APPEAR ON RADAR? A standard 406 MHz EPIRB does NOT create twelve dots on X-band or S-band radar. A radar-SART answers 9 GHz X-band radar interrogations and may appear as a string of 12 dots changing to arcs at close range. S-band radar does not activate radar-SART in this way. AIS-SART and AIS-equipped EPIRBs transmit position on AIS 1/2; a compatible AIS/ECDIS display (or radar display with AIS overlay) may show a special SAR target. This is NOT an X-band radar-SART response. AIS reception depends on line-of-sight and receiver configuration.

Three displays: standard EPIRB no 12 dot.en: Three displays: standard EPIRB no 12 dots, radar SART twelve dots on X band, AIS EPIRB AIS target

Twelve X-band radar dots belong to radar.en: Twelve X-band radar dots belong to radar-SART, not a conventional EPIRB.

A self-test may emit a short specially e.en: A self-test may emit a short specially encoded RF test burst which should not be processed as a real SAR distress alert. Never routinely test by switching to ON/DISTRESS; even one actual 406 MHz burst can trigger rescue coordination.

Ensure the EPIRB is transmitting and is placed upright with a clear sky view; allow the float-free system to function and never lash the beacon to the vessel.

EPIRB — THE DISTRESS ALERT CHAIN An Emer.en: EPIRB — THE DISTRESS ALERT CHAIN An Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon (EPIRB) broadcasts a digital distress signal in the 406–406.1 MHz band. The beacon transmits its unique 15-character HEX ID and, where available, GNSS position. Cospas-Sarsat satellites (LEOSAR, GEOSAR, MEOSAR) relay the alert to a Local User Terminal (LUT), Mission Control Centre (MCC), then the appropriate RCC/MRCC, which coordinates SAR resources. EPIRB is not a two-way VHF voice radio or an automatic marine radar target.

EPIRB → Cospas-Sarsat → LUT → MCC → RCC/.en: EPIRB → Cospas-Sarsat → LUT → MCC → RCC/MRCC → SAR resources.

FLOAT-FREE ACTIVATION AND THE BATTERY A.en: FLOAT-FREE ACTIVATION AND THE BATTERY A float-free EPIRB is mounted in an unobstructed, approved cradle. As the vessel submerges, the Hydrostatic Release Unit (HRU) mechanically opens at approximately 1–4 m depth, depending on the model. The buoyant beacon rises and the water sensor activates its electronics. Seawater does NOT charge or power the battery; a pre-installed sealed battery provides the electrical energy. The beacon can also be activated manually according to its model's instructions. Never tie the buoyant lanyard to the sinking ship. Check for incorrect bracket/magnet/reed-switch placement after service.

GNSS testing may be a separate battery-c.en: GNSS testing may be a separate battery-consuming function; follow the model-specific permitted interval.

HRU releases mechanically; water sensor.en: HRU releases mechanically; water sensor triggers electronics; battery is pre-installed.

MAINTENANCE, REGISTRATION AND FALSE ALER.en: MAINTENANCE, REGISTRATION AND FALSE ALERTS Annual tests are covered by IMO MSC.1/Circ.1040/Rev.2. Shore-based maintenance intervals follow the flag Administration and must not exceed five years under MSC.1/Circ.1039/Rev.1. There is no universal battery or HRU replacement date for every model: check actual expiry and manufacturer-approved instructions. Update the 15 HEX ID registration when the vessel's responsible details change. If accidentally activated without genuine distress, switch OFF immediately and inform the nearest RCC/MRCC with beacon ID, position and time.

A 406 MHz EPIRB alerts Cospas-Sarsat thr.en: A 406 MHz EPIRB alerts Cospas-Sarsat through the satellite/ground network; 121.5 MHz aids local homing. A 9 GHz radar-SART responds to X-band radar, while AIS-SART or AIS-equipped EPIRBs may appear on suitable AIS displays.

Common error: Do not assume 'once on dem.en: Common error: Do not assume 'once on demurrage, always on demurrage' resolves every negotiated exception.

Common error: Never use a live distress.en: Common error: Never use a live distress alert or a radar-SART response as an unplanned test.

A standard EPIRB does not produce radar-.en: A standard EPIRB does not produce radar-SART twelve-dot trails.

Continue monitoring CPA and the other ve.en: Continue monitoring CPA and the other vessel; do not stop assessing once the initial alteration is made.

During an abandon-ship drill, the SART i.en: During an abandon-ship drill, the SART is located but nobody can explain its deployment and activation.

Explain the radar-SART's characteristic.en: Explain the radar-SART's characteristic response to a compatible X-band interrogating radar.

Investigate water treatment, level sensi.en: Investigate water treatment, level sensing and causes only once the boiler is safe and appropriately isolated.
